rules.title: Davis-Bacon applies to federal and federally funded construction contracts over $2,000
rules.plain_english: If a construction, alteration or repair contract (painting and decorating included) is paid for by a federal agency, or with federal grant or loan money under a Davis-Bacon Related Act, and is worth more than $2,000, the federal prevailing wage clauses apply. The $2,000 figure comes from the statute and is never raised for inflation. Subcontracts of any size under a covered prime contract carry the same clauses.

funding_sources: federal loan, grant, loan guarantee or insurance under a Davis-Bacon Related Act

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)

rules.title: Pay every laborer and mechanic on site at least the wage determination rate, at least weekly
rules.plain_english: Everyone doing manual or trade work on the site must be paid at least once a week the full basic hourly rate plus fringe benefits (or the same amount in cash) shown in the wage determination for the work they actually do. Their label (employee, owner-operator, "independent contractor") does not matter. Only deductions allowed by the Copeland Act rules may be taken.

parameters.minimum_hourly_pay: wage determination basic hourly rate + fringe benefit rate (or cash equivalent) for each classification actually worked

rules.source_location: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(1)(i)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.verbatim_quote: All laborers and mechanics employed or working upon the site of the work (or otherwise working in construction or development of the project under a development statute), will be paid unconditionally and not less often than once a week, and without subsequent deduction or rebate on any account (except such payroll deductions as are permitted by regulations issued by the Secretary of Labor under the Copeland Act (29 CFR part 3)), the full amount of basic hourly wages and bona fide fringe benefits (or cash equivalents thereof) due at time of payment computed at rates not less than those contained in the wage determination of the Secretary of Labor which is attached hereto and made a part hereof, regardless of any contractual relationship which may be alleged to exist between the contractor and such laborers and mechanics.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Direct federal (FAR) contracts use FAR 52.222-6 (AUG 2018), which has the same weekly-pay rule. California public works law (Labor Code 1771 et seq.) still applies on top when a California awarding body controls the project (see fed-ca-dual-coverage-pay-higher).

rules.title: Workers in more than one trade may be paid each trade's rate only if payroll shows hours in each
rules.plain_english: If a worker does work in two or more classifications (for example laborer and operator), you may pay the rate for each classification for the hours spent in it, but only if your payroll records accurately show the time in each one. Otherwise expect to owe the highest rate for all hours.

rules.title: Missing trade on the wage determination: request a conformed rate; DOL answers in 30 days
rules.plain_english: If you will use a type of worker that is not listed on the wage determination, the contracting officer must get an added ("conformed") classification and rate. DOL approves, changes or rejects it within 30 days of receipt (or says it needs more time). Once set, the rate must be paid back to the first day anyone worked in that classification, and you must give each affected worker a written copy or post it with the wage determination.

rules.title: Back wages owed under Davis-Bacon carry interest (IRS underpayment rate, compounded daily)
rules.plain_english: If any prevailing wages are underpaid, the contractor must also pay interest from the date of the underpayment. The interest rate is the IRS rate for underpaid taxes (26 U.S.C. 6621), compounded daily.

rules.title: Agency can withhold your payments, including on your other federal jobs, to cover unpaid wages
rules.plain_english: If you or any subcontractor underpay prevailing wages, the agency (or the city/Caltrans paying with federal money) may, and must if DOL asks in writing, hold back enough of your contract payments to cover the wages, interest and relief. It can also hold money on any other federal or federally assisted contract held by the same prime contractor, even with a different agency. Failing to pay or to submit payroll records can stop all further payments after written notice.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
